newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope sees need for large-scale operation in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Pope sees need for large-scale operation in Zaire.

text.p: Pope John Paul on Wednesday said a multinational force for eastern Zaire should go ahead even though 500,000 Rwandan refugees had returned home.
Speaking at his weekly general audience at the Vatican, the Pope said the "tragic situation" in the Great Lakes region of Africa was in his thoughts and prayers.
The Pope noted that many Rwandan Hutu refugees had returned home in the past days, but said "immediate and large-scale actions" were still needed.
He made a specific appeal to countries which have agreed to participate in the Canadian-led force, originally intended to help feed refugees in Zaire and help them return home.
Several of the participants are now rethinking its mandate after 500,000 refugees returned to Rwanda since November 15.
Military planners from these countries have called a meeting in Stuttgart, Germany, to review the mission.

"I hope in my prayers that the meeting of representatives of the multinational force in Stuttgart on Friday could help to avoid additional suffering, ensuring respect, safety and needed assistance for all," the Pope said.
The Pope joined humanitarian organisations which have said there were still another 500,000 or more Hutu refugees in eastern Zaire whose whereabouts were in question.
"Many have remained with no help whatsoever and wander in the forests of eastern Zaire, in need of everything," he said.
The U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) said that an estimated 100,000 more refugees were on the move on Wednesday from the Bukavu area and were heading north towards Goma, near the Rwandan border.
